evidence.note: Agent enumerates the major subsystems (package.json, CLI bin, Vite plugin/next-* resolution, runtime shims, route scanner, SSR/SSG server, client hydration) and orders scaffolding before implementation — identifying real subsystems, but as a flat component list with no dependency-aware ordering and no per-subsystem done-criteria.

All subsystems are written in one batched push and built once, then validated against the full 335-test suite at once, rather than sequencing a minimal end-to-end route-under-dev slice and gating each milestone on targeted tests.

Thorough up-front understanding of tests/fixtures/shims, but the resulting 'Plan' lines are next-action notes ('write implementation source in batches', 'then iterate by running tests'), not an ordered milestone plan tied to concrete verifiable checkpoints.

After the single full-suite run hangs, the agent spends the entire remainder trapped trying to recover a wedged terminal; the initial decomposition is never revisited or re-planned, so no living/dependency-managed sequencing over the horizon exists.

reasoning: The agent correctly identifies the major subsystems and applies a rough scaffold-first-then-implement ordering, which lifts it above the flat requirement-bullet list of anchor 3. But it stops short of anchor 5's dependency-aware sequencing: there is no minimal end-to-end vertical slice built before layering features, no per-milestone done-criteria, and validation was a single big-bang full-suite run rather than incremental gating. The plan was never revisited (the whole back half is terminal-recovery flailing), so the self-correcting, living decomposition of the higher anchors is absent — placing the observed behavior at a 4, between the flat-list 3 and the subsystem-ordering 5.
